scope: Deterministic scroll instance-byte attribution and pixel correctness; no CPU, latency or hardware-performance claim.

provenance.execution: Headless Chromium ANGLE SwiftShader; deterministic byte/correctness only; no timing measurements

configuration.host: actual comparison-entry.ts createNative -> TerminalSession -> DOM host -> WebGlTerminalRenderer

treatment.baseline: Isolated instance override notifyScroll() -> existing private invalidateAll(); all other source is final source. This reproduces the previous scroll full-rebuild behavior, not a checked-out historical release.
treatment.final: Unmodified final renderer notifyScroll all-row refresh; Zig compares persistent records and emits changed ranges.
treatment.oracle: Unmodified renderer with existing zigFrame:false option; complete JavaScript producer.

definitions.rows: Identical means exact byte equality at the same viewport row across a scroll/frame. Whole = both buffers; glyph = 96-byte glyph records; cellBackground = 64-byte cell records (background/decoration data). Text compares padded 40-column rows read from the current render-state snapshot. The DOM host visibleLines() is latched after upload and is deliberately not used at that boundary.
definitions.changedRecords: Exact raw record changes at fixed viewport positions, independently in each buffer; unionColumns counts positions changed in either buffer.
definitions.uploadedRecords: Extent of emitted ranges, not count of records that differ. Actual gl.bufferSubData arguments separately confirm byte lengths and calls.
definitions.unchangedRecords: Unchanged complete records inside uploaded ranges, including cell/background records. Unchanged bytes within a changed record are not classified as separate wasted records.
definitions.trailingBlankUnchanged: Uploaded record unchanged and its column lies after trimEnd() for both old and new text. Distinct from spaces inside authored text.
definitions.interiorUnchanged: Unchanged uploaded record strictly between first and last changed records in that range. This measures the holes inside the contiguous bounding range.
definitions.afterTrailingBlankRecords: Uploaded columns after new row text end, including erasures whose previous glyph differed; erasures are necessary, not automatically wasted.
definitions.pixelParity: SHA-256 of readPixels called immediately after the actual scheduled pass.submit; no capturePixels or forced redraw. A skipped native submit retains its previously submitted image. All eight operations per workload must match full JS oracle; final displayed canvas screenshot is separately compared.
definitions.scrollCalls: Actual DOM-host notifyScroll calls within each operation. Output frames can contain many parser line scrolls but one host notification and one coalesced scheduled paint.
definitions.buildCalls: Actual Zig builder calls; status 2 requests missing-glyph registration, status 0 succeeds. bridge_build_frame forces full row ranges on a missing-glyph retry to retain changes written by its first pass, even when fullRequested is false. This is a correctness guard.
definitions.totals: totals includes captured driver-reset operations so it exactly reconciles renderer metrics. outputOrScrollTotals excludes driver-reset and covers the eight output/scroll operations.

rolling.reset: corpus-start for each burst, including separately reset warmup
rolling.unicodePreserved: Original en dash remains in corpus and measured input; fallback metrics record displayed-frame producer

limitations: Eight deterministic output frames and eight one-row viewport scrolls per workload; exact output driver workload and chunk size, not the full 2700-frame timing run.
One terminal. Instance bytes/calls are additive for 17 identical terminals; this proof makes no scheduling or timing claim at 17.
Uniform black backgrounds/white foreground, hidden cursor, no selection. Changing per-row background/style can invalidate cell records and reduce savings.
Headless software WebGL for correctness. Raw record comparison and buffer arguments are independent of GPU speed.
Baseline is a one-method counterfactual using final producer/source; historical native17 trace is supporting provenance, not an equivalent fresh historical execution.
Final displayed pixels verified after the workload; every intermediate submitted frame uses immediate backbuffer readback, not compositor screenshots for every frame.

assessment.verdict: The large repeated-fixture reduction does not generalize in magnitude to distinct scrolling text. A material uniform-background byte reduction does generalize; all-row refresh remains correct when every visible glyph changes.
assessment.stockGitLogs: The entire 24643-byte normalized history unit is sent on every stock logs frame; its final viewport also repeats. Seven steady measured output frames upload zero bytes, so this fixture is not an independent distinct-output generalization check.

distinctFull40History.sourceOfSaving: Only unchanged cell/background records; no repeated glyph records or blank tails.

assessment.distinctFull40Output: After the first missing-glyph registration retry, each frame uploads 42240 glyph bytes in 11 calls. Eleven full rows change and the CRLF-created bottom blank row stays identical. The 45% steady saving is 40% unchanged backgrounds plus 5% bottom blank glyph row.
assessment.raggedRanges: Normal changed-range frames exclude unchanged blank tails. They still upload unchanged interior glyph records between the first and last changed columns. Changed zero-glyph records after a shortened line erase its old tail and are necessary; they are distinguished from unchanged blanks.
assessment.missingGlyphRetries: Recorded status-2 retries conservatively upload full row ranges even with fullRequested=false. Their full cell/background and trailing-blank uploads are retained in actual totals, not removed from the evidence.
assessment.design: Evidence supports the simple all-row refresh correction. It does not support interpreting zero-upload repeated output as generic scroll cost or adding new heuristics from this byte-only proof.

rollingGitLogs.unicode: The en dash is preserved in the consumed input and corpus. Fallback is counted only when unsupported content is visible in a sampled frame; zero fallback here does not mean Zig supports that codepoint.

invariants: Actual buffer-call offsets and lengths equal every emitted range
Actual buffer-call bytes equal emitted bytes per kind/frame
Actual buffer-call counts equal renderer upload operations
Summed frame bytes/calls equal renderer metric deltas
Baseline/final changed-record counts and identical-row classifications match
Every measured operation matches complete JS oracle readback and visible text
Final displayed screenshots match complete JS oracle
No native frames fell back to JS
